## 🎯 **STEP 2: Understanding the Labor Revenue Logic**

This is the key insight I was missing! Let me confirm I understand correctly:

**The business logic is:**

- Find all work orders that HAVE an inspection (at least one inspection job code)
- Sum ALL labor from those work orders (both inspection and non-inspection jobs)
- That's "Labor With Inspection"
- Then subtract out just the inspection job labor to get "Labor $$"

**Your measures:**

dax

```dax
Labor With Inspection = 
VAR InspectionWOs = 
    CALCULATETABLE(
        VALUES(Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber]),
        Fact_LaborJobSummary[IsInspection] = TRUE
    )
RETURN
    CALCULATE(
        SUM(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoicedLaborAmount]),
        Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber] IN InspectionWOs
    )

Labor $$ = [Labor With Inspection] - [Inspection $$]
```

## ✅ **Confirming Your Measures**

### **1. Total Inspections** - Your measure is PERFECT!

dax

```dax
Total Inspections = 
CALCULATE(
    COUNTROWS(Fact_LaborJobSummary),  
    Fact_LaborJobSummary[IsInspection] = TRUE
)
```

**Why this works:**

- Grain = one row per JobCode per WorkOrder
- Each inspection creates ONE row with IsInspection = TRUE
- COUNTROWS counts those inspection job rows
- If 1,345 inspections performed, there are 1,345 rows with IsInspection = TRUE ✓

**My SUMMARIZE approach was unnecessary** because your grain is already at JobCode level. Your simple approach is more efficient!

---

### **2. Labor With Inspection** - PERFECT!

dax

```dax
Labor With Inspection = 
VAR InspectionWOs = 
    CALCULATETABLE(
        VALUES(Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber]),
        Fact_LaborJobSummary[IsInspection] = TRUE
    )
RETURN
    CALCULATE(
        SUM(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoicedLaborAmount]),
        Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber] IN InspectionWOs
    )
```

**Example with WO 662026:**

- InspectionWOs = {662026} (has at least one IsInspection=TRUE row)
- Labor With Inspection = SUM of all 25 job rows for WO 662026
- This includes the $213.5 inspection labor + all other labor

**Exactly right!** ✓

---

### **3. Labor $$ and Inspection $$** - PERFECT!

dax

```dax
Inspection $$ = 
CALCULATE(
    SUM(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoicedLaborAmount]),
    Fact_LaborJobSummary[IsInspection] = TRUE
)

Labor $$ = [Labor With Inspection] - [Inspection $$]
```

**Example with WO 662026:**

- Inspection $$ = $213.5 (just the IS-TRACTOR INSPECT row)
- Labor $$ = (all 25 rows) - (inspection row) = the other 24 jobs' labor

**Perfect logic!** ✓

Ok, I have a question about the hours, does this take into account the fact that more hours may have been worked on the work order, or is it just the hours worked on the specific inspection job code? Let's go back to the examples I showed you earlier, that one work order had 25 lines of service work, 24 of them were because the Inspection happened. Can we capture both of these? Recognized parallel metrics needed for comprehensive inspection labor tracking.

**BRILLIANT QUESTION!** 🎯 Yes, absolutely - this makes perfect sense and follows the **exact same logic** as your Labor revenue measures!

---

## 💡 **The Parallel Logic**

### **Labor Revenue (what you already have):**

dax

```dax
Inspection $$ = Just the inspection job labor
Labor With Inspection = ALL labor on WOs that have inspections
Labor $$ = Labor With Inspection - Inspection $$
```

### **Hours (what you need):**

dax

```dax
Hours Worked (Inspection) = Just the inspection job hours
Hours Worked With Inspection = ALL hours on WOs that have inspections
Additional Hours from Inspection = Hours With Inspection - Hours Worked (Inspection)
```

**Same concept!** You want to measure the **full labor commitment** generated by inspections, not just the inspection itself.

---

## 📊 **Using WO 662026 as Example**

From your screenshots:

**The Work Order:**

- 1 inspection job: IS-TRACTOR INSPECT
- 24 other jobs: DAILY SERVICE, Gen-Electrical, etc.

**What You Want to Track:**

|Metric|Value|Meaning|
|---|---|---|
|Hours Worked (Inspection)|~2-3 hrs?|Just the IS-TRACTOR INSPECT job|
|Hours Worked With Inspection|~20-30 hrs?|All 25 jobs combined|
|Additional Hours|~18-27 hrs?|The 24 other jobs|

**Business Insight:** "We did a 3-hour inspection and it generated 25 hours of additional work!" 🎯

## ✅ **Recommended Measures - Full Set**

### **Inspection Hours Only** (Current logic)

dax

```dax
Hours Worked = 
CALCULATE(
    SUM(Fact_LaborJobSummary[ActualHoursWorked]),
    Fact_LaborJobSummary[IsInspection] = TRUE
)

Hours Invoiced = 
CALCULATE(
    SUM(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoicedHours]),
    Fact_LaborJobSummary[IsInspection] = TRUE
)
```

---

### **Total Hours on Inspection Work Orders** (NEW - mirrors Labor With Inspection)

dax

```dax
Hours Worked With Inspection = 
VAR InspectionWOs = 
    CALCULATETABLE(
        VALUES(Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber]),
        Fact_LaborJobSummary[IsInspection] = TRUE
    )
RETURN
    CALCULATE(
        SUM(Fact_LaborJobSummary[ActualHoursWorked]),
        Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber] IN InspectionWOs
    )

Hours Invoiced With Inspection = 
VAR InspectionWOs = 
    CALCULATETABLE(
        VALUES(Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber]),
        Fact_LaborJobSummary[IsInspection] = TRUE
    )
RETURN
    CALCULATE(
        SUM(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoicedHours]),
        Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber] IN InspectionWOs
    )
```

---

### **Additional Hours Generated** (NEW - shows the upsell)

dax

```dax
Additional Hours Worked = 
[Hours Worked With Inspection] - [Hours Worked]

Additional Hours Invoiced = 
[Hours Invoiced With Inspection] - [Hours Invoiced]
```

### **STEP 1: Total Inspection Goals** (All Inspections)

dax

```dax

// TOTAL INSPECTION GOALS

Total Inspection Goal = 
CALCULATE(
    SUM('Inspection Goals'[2025 Inspections Goal]),
    TREATAS(
        VALUES(Dim_BranchLocation[BranchCode]),
        'Inspection Goals'[LOCATION]
    )
)

Labor With Inspection Goal =

    SUM('Inspection Goals'[2025 Labor $$ w/ Inspection Goal]),
    TREATAS(

        'Inspection Goals'[LOCATION]
    )
)

Parts Goal = 
CALCULATE(
    SUM('Inspection Goals'[2025 Total Parts $$ Goal]),
    TREATAS(
        VALUES(Dim_BranchLocation[BranchCode]),
        'Inspection Goals'[LOCATION]
    )
)

// % to Goal Calculations
% to Goal - Inspections = 
DIVIDE(
    [Total Inspections],
    [Total Inspection Goal],
    0
)

% to Goal - Labor With Inspection = 
DIVIDE(
    [Labor With Inspection],
    [Labor With Inspection Goal],
    0
)

    [Parts $ Total],
    [Parts Goal],

)
```

### **STEP 2: CS690-CS770 Specific Measures** (5 Job Codes)

dax

```dax
// ============================================================================
// CS690-CS770 SPECIFIC TRACKING (5 JOB CODES)
// ============================================================================

CS690-CS770 Inspections = 
CALCULATE(
    COUNTROWS(Fact_LaborJobSummary),
    Fact_LaborJobSummary[IsInspection] = TRUE,
    Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode] IN {
        "IS-CS690 INSPECT",
        "IS-CS770 INSPECT",
        "IS-STRIPPER INSPECT",
        "IS-CP690 INSPECT",
        "IS-CP770 INSPECT"
    }
)

CS690-CS770 Labor With Inspection = 
VAR CS690WOs = 
    CALCULATETABLE(
        VALUES(Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber]),
        Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode] IN {
            "IS-CS690 INSPECT",
            "IS-CS770 INSPECT",
            "IS-STRIPPER INSPECT",
            "IS-CP690 INSPECT",
            "IS-CP770 INSPECT"
        }
    )
RETURN
    CALCULATE(
        SUM(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoicedLaborAmount]),
        Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber] IN CS690WOs
    )

CS690-CS770 Parts Total = 
VAR CS690Invoices = 
    CALCULATETABLE(
        VALUES(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoiceNumber]),
        Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode] IN {
            "IS-CS690 INSPECT",
            "IS-CS770 INSPECT",
            "IS-STRIPPER INSPECT",
            "IS-CP690 INSPECT",
            "IS-CP770 INSPECT"
        },
        NOT(ISBLANK(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoiceNumber]))
    )
RETURN
    CALCULATE(
        SUM(Fact_WorkOrderParts[SaleValue]),
        Fact_WorkOrderParts[InvoiceNumber] IN CS690Invoices,
        Fact_WorkOrderParts[Franchise] <> "ZP",
        NOT(Fact_WorkOrderParts[PartNumber] IN {"ADV", "LEGACY", "4900", "*10PROMO"})
    )
```

## 🔍 **Understanding the Pending Inspections Logic**

### **What "Pending" Means:**

From your old report logic:

- Work orders that **have an inspection job code** (HasInspectionJobCode = 1)
- That are **not yet completed** (still in RepairOrderDetail with pending status)
- Need to show hours worked from TechnicianPunchedDetail

### **Key Insight:**

**RepairOrderDetail ≠ Fact_LaborJobSummary**

|Table|Scope|Grain|
|---|---|---|
|Fact_LaborJobSummary|Jobs that are invoiced/in wkothsub|One row per **job code**|
|RepairOrderDetail|**ALL work orders** (including not started)|One row per **work order**|

**This is why you need both!** RepairOrderDetail has work orders that haven't made it to wkothsub yet.

---

## 💡 **My Recommendation: Create Fact_PendingInspections**

**Why a separate fact table is best:**

✅ **Different Grain:**

- Fact_LaborJobSummary = Job level (multiple jobs per WO)
- Fact_PendingInspections = Work Order level (one row per WO)

✅ **Different Purpose:**

- Fact_LaborJobSummary = Completed/invoiced work
- Fact_PendingInspections = Work not yet completed

✅ **Performance:**

- Won't slow down your existing fact tables
- Only processes pending records (much smaller dataset)
- Can pre-aggregate hours from TechnicianPunchedDetail

✅ **Simplicity:**

- Clean separation of concerns
- Easy DAX measures (no complex filtering)
- Clear for future developers

❌ **Why NOT to extend Fact_LaborJobSummary:**

- Already complex (3 raw table joins)
- Different grain would cause confusion
- Would significantly slow refresh time
- Business logic is fundamentally different

---

## 🏗️ **Proposed Fact_PendingInspections Architecture**

### **Grain:** One row per pending work order with inspection

### **Data Flow:**

```
Raw_RepairOrderDetail (all WOs)
    └─> Filter to inspection job codes
        └─> Filter to pending statuses
            └─> Left join Raw_TechnicianPunchedDetail (aggregate hours)
                └─> Fact_PendingInspections
```

### **Structure (12-15 columns):**

```
Core Identifiers:
- BranchCode
- WorkOrderNumber
- JobCode (the inspection job code)
- JobType

Status & Timeline:
- StatusDisplay
- ROProgressStatus
- CreationDate
- LastLaborPunch
- DaysSinceCreation (age)

Hours Data:
- HoursWorked (from TechnicianPunchedDetail)
- HoursInternal (breakdown)
- HoursWarranty (breakdown)
- HoursRetail (breakdown)

Flags:
- IsInspection (always TRUE in this table)
```

Verified query captures all work order hours comprehensively.

---

## 📊 **What the Query Captures:**

Looking at **Step 5** in the query:

m

````m
AggregateHours = Table.Group(
    TechHoursSource,
    {"Branch", "WorkOrder"},  // ← Groups by Work Order
    {
        {"HoursWorked", each List.Sum([HoursWorked]), type nullable number}  // ← Sums ALL hours
    }
),
```

**This sums ALL hours for the entire work order** - not just inspection job code hours.

---

## 💡 **Why This is Correct for Pending Inspections:**

### **The Context:**
- **RepairOrderDetail** = Work Order level (one row per WO)
- Has ONE primary JobCode (the inspection in this case)
- But the WO can have multiple jobs/tech punches

### **Example Pending Work Order:**
```
WO 661073 (Pending)
├─ JobCode: IS-TRACTOR INSPECT (primary - shows in RepairOrderDetail)
├─ Tech Punch 1: 2 hours (on the inspection)
├─ Tech Punch 2: 3 hours (started other work)
└─ Tech Punch 3: 1 hour (parts-related work)

Total Hours Worked: 6 hours ← This is what we show
````

**This matches your old report logic:**

dax

```dax
HoursWorked = 
VAR Hours = 
    SUMX(
        FILTER(
            TechnicianPunchedDetail, 
            TechnicianPunchedDetail[RepairOrderNumber] = RepairOrderDetail[RONumber]
        ), 
        TechnicianPunchedDetail[HoursWorked]  // ← ALL hours for the WO
    )
```

---

## ✅ **This is What You Want Because:**

1. **Shows work progress** on the pending inspection
2. **Includes all labor** happening on that work order
3. **Mirrors your labor revenue logic** (Labor With Inspection = all labor on inspection WOs)
4. **Business insight:** "This inspection WO has 6 hours invested so far"

---

## 🤔 **If You Wanted ONLY Inspection Job Code Hours:**

You would need to filter in the aggregation step:

m

```m
// This would only sum hours WHERE JobCode is the inspection
AggregateHours = Table.Group(
    Table.SelectRows(TechHoursSource, each [JobCode] = [inspection_code]),  // ← Add filter
    {"Branch", "WorkOrder"},
    {
        {"HoursWorked", each List.Sum([HoursWorked]), type nullable number}
    }
),
```

**But I don't think you want this!**

- Font size: **64pt** (make it BIG!)
- Font: Segoe UI (or your preference)
- Color: `#333333` (dark gray)
- Display units: None
- Decimal places: 0

**Step 1.6: Format the label:**

- **Category label** section
- Text: "Total Inspections"
- Font size: **18pt**
- Font weight: Semi-bold
- Color: `#666666`
- Position: Above the number

**Step 1.7: Add reference labels (the context):**

- Click **Reference labels** → Add
- **Label 1:** Total Inspection Goal
    - Position: Bottom
    - Prefix: "Goal: "
    - Font size: 14pt
- **Label 2:** % to Goal - Inspections
    - Position: Bottom (next to Label 1)
    - Prefix: " | "
    - Suffix: " to Goal"
    - Font size: 14pt
    - Color: `#28A745` (green)

**Step 1.8: Card styling:**

- **Effects** → Background: On
- Background color: White or very light gray (`#F8F9FA`)
- **Effects** → Border: On
- Border color: `#E0E0E0`
- Border weight: 1px
- **Effects** → Rounded corners: 8px
- **Effects** → Shadow: On (subtle drop shadow, optional)

## 🎨 **The Problem: Too Much Horizontal Space**

With a 1664px wide canvas, a full-width card with just 2 elements (title + number) creates too much emptiness.

---

## 💡 **Solution: Two Quick Fixes**

### **Fix #1: Add the Reference Labels NOW** (fills the vertical space)

Let's add the context below the number to fill out the card:

**Add Reference Labels:**

1. Click on the card visual
2. Format pane → **Reference labels** → Turn ON
3. Click **+ Add**

**Reference Label 1 - Goal:**

- Data field: **Total Inspection Goal**
- Text: Custom
- Prefix text: "Goal: "
- Font size: 16pt
- Color: `#666666` (gray)
- Horizontal alignment: Center
- Vertical position: Below value

**Reference Label 2 - % to Goal:**

- Data field: **% to Goal - Inspections**
- Text: Custom
- Format: Percentage
- Suffix text: " to Goal"
- Font size: 18pt
- Font weight: Bold
- Color: `#28A745` (green)
- Horizontal alignment: Center
- Vertical position: Below value

**Reference Label 3 - Above Goal Count** (optional):

- Create a quick measure: `Inspections Above Goal = [Total Inspections] - [Total Inspection Goal]`
- Prefix: "+"
- Suffix: " above goal"
- Font size: 14pt
- Color: `#28A745` (green)

This will fill the vertical space better!

---

### **Fix #2: Reduce Card Width** (less horizontal stretching)

Instead of full width, try:

- **Width: ~1000-1100px** (about 60-65% of canvas width)
- **Center it horizontally** on the page
- Leaves breathing room on sides

**Or even better - split into 2 sections side-by-side:**

```
┌────────── HERO ──────────┐  ┌──── SUMMARY ────┐
│ Total Inspections        │  │ Revenue: $11.09M │
│                          │  │ Hours: 28K       │
│      1,421               │  │ Pending: 80      │
│                          │  │                  │
│ Goal: 1,083 | 131% ↑     │  │                  │
└──────────────────────────┘  └──────────────────┘
```

---

## 🎯 **My Recommendation: Try This Layout**

Given your wide canvas, let's use a **3-column top section** instead of one wide card:

```
┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐
│  Total       │  │  Revenue     │  │  Performance │
│  Inspections │  │  Generated   │  │  vs Goal     │
│              │  │              │  │              │
│    1,421     │  │  $11.09M     │  │    131%      │
│              │  │              │  │              │
│ +341 above   │  │ All sources  │  │ [progress]   │
└──────────────┘  └──────────────┘  └──────────────┘
```

**Three equal-width cards (~500px each)** would look much better on your wide canvas than one stretched-out card.

## 🎯 **STEP 2: Create the HTML Measure**

## 🎨 **OPTION 1: Modern Card with Gradient Accent**

### **Create this DAX measure:**

dax

```dax
Hero Card HTML = 
VAR Inspections = [Total Inspections]
VAR Goal = [Total Inspection Goal]
VAR Pct = [% to Goal - Inspections]
VAR Above = Inspections - Goal
VAR PctText = FORMAT(Pct, "0%")
VAR AboveText = FORMAT(Above, "+#,##0;-#,##0")
VAR Revenue = [Inspection $$] + [Parts $ Total] + [Labor $$]
VAR RevenueText = FORMAT(Revenue / 1000000, "$#,##0.0") & "M"

RETURN
"
<div style='
    font-family: Segoe UI, Arial, sans-serif;
    padding: 30px;
    background: linear-gradient(135deg, #667eea 0%, #764ba2 100%);
    border-radius: 12px;
    box-shadow: 0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.15);
    color: white;
    height: 180px;
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    justify-content: space-around;
'>
    <!-- Main Metric -->
    <div style='text-align: center; flex: 1;'>
        <div style='font-size: 14px; opacity: 0.9; margin-bottom: 10px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 1px;'>
            Total Inspections
        </div>
        <div style='font-size: 72px; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1;'>
            " & FORMAT(Inspections, "#,##0") & "
        </div>
        <div style='font-size: 18px; margin-top: 10px; opacity: 0.9;'>
            Goal: " & FORMAT(Goal, "#,##0") & " | " & PctText & " ↑
        </div>
    </div>
    
    <!-- Divider -->
    <div style='width: 2px; height: 120px; background: rgba(255,255,255,0.3); margin: 0 40px;'></div>
    
    <!-- Revenue -->
    <div style='text-align: center; flex: 1;'>
        <div style='font-size: 14px; opacity: 0.9; margin-bottom: 10px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 1px;'>
            Total Revenue
        </div>
        <div style='font-size: 56px; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1;'>
            " & RevenueText & "
        </div>
        <div style='font-size: 16px; margin-top: 10px; opacity: 0.9;'>
            Inspection + Parts + Labor
        </div>
    </div>
    
    <!-- Divider -->
    <div style='width: 2px; height: 120px; background: rgba(255,255,255,0.3); margin: 0 40px;'></div>
    
    <!-- Performance Badge -->
    <div style='text-align: center; flex: 1;'>
        <div style='font-size: 14px; opacity: 0.9; margin-bottom: 10px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 1px;'>
            Performance
        </div>
        <div style='
            font-size: 64px; 
            font-weight: 700; 
            line-height: 1;
            color: #4ade80;
        '>
            " & PctText & "
        </div>
        <div style='font-size: 18px; margin-top: 10px; font-weight: 600;'>
            " & AboveText & " above goal
        </div>
    </div>
</div>
"
```

**Result:** Beautiful purple gradient card with 3 sections - modern and eye-catching!

## 📋 **How to Implement:**

**Step 1:** Create ONE of these measures (try Option 3 first - it's my favorite!)

**Step 2:** Add the HTML Content visual to your canvas

**Step 3:** Drag the measure into the visual's **Values** field

**Step 4:** Size it:

- Width: 1400-1500px (almost full width)
- Height: 180-200px
- Position at top of page

**Step 5:** Admire! 🎉

````dax
- **Parts card:** Green pill badge showing **152% ↑**
- **Labor card:** Blue pill badge showing **149% ↑**
- Positioned **next to the main number** (not in footer)
- Color-matched to border (green for parts, blue for labor)
- **Cards without goals:** No badge (keeps it clean)

```
┌─────────────────────┐

│                     │
│ [Context message]   │  ← Explanation stays in footer
└─────────────────────┘
```

## 🎯 **Why This Layout Works:**

- ✅ Immediately visible

- ✅ Color-coded for quick scanning (green/blue)

**Footer stays focused:**
- ✅ Explains **what** the number means
- ✅ Shows the **math** breakdown
- ✅ No competing information
````

```
AverageLaborAndParts = 
DIVIDE (
    [TestTotalLaborWithInspection] + [Parts $ Total],
    [DistinctInspectionJobCodesCount]
)
```

```
AverageLaborDiscount = 
DIVIDE ( [TestTotalLaborDiscount], [DistinctInspectionJobCodesCount] )
```

```
AverageLaborWithInspection = 
DIVIDE ( [TestTotalLaborWithInspection], [DistinctInspectionJobCodesCount] )
```

```
AveragePartDiscountPerInspection = 
DIVIDE ( [Parts Discount], [DistinctInspectionJobCodesCount] )
```

```
AveragePartsPerInspection = 
DIVIDE ( [Parts $ Total], [DistinctInspectionJobCodesCount] )
```

```
AveragePercentDiscounted = 
DIVIDE (
    ABS ( [TestTotalLaborDiscount] + [Parts Discount] ),
    [TestTotalLaborWithInspection] + [Parts $ Total]
)
```

```
DistinctInspectionJobCodesCount = 
SUMX (
    VALUES ( 'Job_Code_Times'[wo_number] ),
    CALCULATE (
        DISTINCTCOUNT ( 'Job_Code_Times'[job_code] ),
        'Job_Code_Times'[job_code] IN VALUES ( JobCodes[job_code] )
    )
)
```

```
TestTotalLaborDiscount = [TotalLaborDiscount] * [DistinctInspectionJobCodesCount]
```

```
TestTotalLaborWithInspection = 
SUMX (
    FILTER (
        'DistinctLaborValuesByWoNumber',
        'DistinctLaborValuesByWoNumber'[wo_number]
            IN VALUES ( 'Job_Code_Times'[wo_number] )
                && 'DistinctLaborValuesByWoNumber'[HasInspectionJobCode] = 1
    ),
    'DistinctLaborValuesByWoNumber'[TotalInv_Lab_Val]
)
```

```
TotalMinusDiscounts = 
[TestTotalLaborWithInspection] + [Parts $ Total] + [TestTotalLaborDiscount] + [Parts Discount]
```

## 📊 **Step 1: Understanding Your Data Structure**

### **What You Have:**

**Fact_LaborJobSummary** has rows like this:

```
BranchCode | WorkOrderNumber | JobCode           | InvoicedLaborAmount | IsInspection
11         | 669579          | IS-CS690 INSPECT  | $427                | TRUE
11         | 669579          | Gen-Electrical    | $385                | FALSE
11         | 669579          | DAILY SERVICE     | $290                | FALSE
11         | 662660          | IS-CS690 INSPECT  | $380                | TRUE
11         | 662660          | Parts Work        | $295                | FALSE
```

**The grain:** One row per job code per work order

## 🎯 **Step 2: Building Page 1 - The Summary Table**

### **What We're Creating:**

A table that groups/aggregates by Branch + Job Code:

```
Branch | Job Code         | Count | Parts $ Total | Labor $ Total | Avg Parts | Avg Labor
11     | IS-CS690 INSPECT | 5     | $43,352      | $39,602       | $8,670    | $7,920
```

### **The "Count" Calculation:**

This is **COUNT of work orders that have this inspection**, not count of rows!

Your `DistinctInspectionJobCodesCount` measure does this:

dax

```dax
DistinctInspectionJobCodesCount = 
SUMX (
    VALUES ( 'Job_Code_Times'[wo_number] ),  // For each unique work order
    CALCULATE (
        DISTINCTCOUNT ( 'Job_Code_Times'[job_code] ),  // Count inspection codes
        'Job_Code_Times'[job_code] IN VALUES ( JobCodes[job_code] )
    )
)
```

**In English:**

- Look at each unique work order
- Count how many inspection job codes it has
- Sum them up

**For our example:**

- WO 669579 has 1 CS690 = 1
- WO 662660 has 1 CS690 = 1
- WO 658568 has 1 CS690 = 1
- WO 661234 has 1 CS690 = 1
- WO 663445 has 1 CS690 = 1
- **Total = 5** ✓

## 🔴 **The Problem:**

When you put `Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode]` in a table visual:

- **Labor measures work** (they're in the same table)
- **Parts measures fail** (they're in Fact_WorkOrderParts with no direct relationship to JobCode)
- Every row shows the same Parts $ total (the grand total) because DAX can't filter it by JobCode

---

## 💡 **The Solution: Bridge Through Work Orders**

We need measures that:

1. Look at the JobCode in the current row
2. Find all work orders that have that JobCode
3. Get the invoice numbers for those work orders
4. Sum parts from those invoices

**This is a CALCULATE pattern with virtual relationships!**

---

## 🛠️ **Step-by-Step: Create New Measures for the New Report**

### **MEASURE 1: Inspection Count (by Job Code)**

dax

```dax
Inspection Count by Job Code = 
VAR CurrentJobCode = SELECTEDVALUE(Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode])
VAR WorkOrdersWithThisJobCode = 
    CALCULATETABLE(
        VALUES(Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber]),
        Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode] = CurrentJobCode,
        Fact_LaborJobSummary[IsInspection] = TRUE
    )
RETURN
    COUNTROWS(WorkOrdersWithThisJobCode)
```

**What this does:**

- Gets the current JobCode from the row context
- Finds all work orders that have this job code AND it's an inspection
- Counts unique work orders

---

### **MEASURE 2: Parts $ Total (for this Job Code)**

dax

```dax
Parts $ by Job Code = 
VAR CurrentJobCode = SELECTEDVALUE(Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode])
VAR WorkOrdersWithThisJobCode = 
    CALCULATETABLE(
        VALUES(Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber]),
        Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode] = CurrentJobCode,
        Fact_LaborJobSummary[IsInspection] = TRUE
    )
VAR InvoicesForTheseWOs = 
    CALCULATETABLE(
        VALUES(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoiceNumber]),
        Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber] IN WorkOrdersWithThisJobCode,
        NOT(ISBLANK(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoiceNumber]))
    )
RETURN
    CALCULATE(
        SUM(Fact_WorkOrderParts[SaleValue]),
        Fact_WorkOrderParts[InvoiceNumber] IN InvoicesForTheseWOs,
        Fact_WorkOrderParts[Franchise] <> "ZP",
        NOT(Fact_WorkOrderParts[PartNumber] IN {"ADV", "LEGACY", "4900", "*10PROMO"})
    )
```

**What this does:**

- Gets work orders with this job code
- Gets invoice numbers for those work orders
- Sums parts from those invoices
- Excludes discount parts

---

### **MEASURE 3: Parts Discount (for this Job Code)**

dax

```dax
Parts Discount by Job Code = 
VAR CurrentJobCode = SELECTEDVALUE(Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode])
VAR WorkOrdersWithThisJobCode = 
    CALCULATETABLE(
        VALUES(Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber]),
        Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode] = CurrentJobCode,
        Fact_LaborJobSummary[IsInspection] = TRUE
    )
VAR InvoicesForTheseWOs = 
    CALCULATETABLE(
        VALUES(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoiceNumber]),
        Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber] IN WorkOrdersWithThisJobCode,
        NOT(ISBLANK(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoiceNumber]))
    )
RETURN
    CALCULATE(
        SUM(Fact_WorkOrderParts[SaleValue]),
        Fact_WorkOrderParts[InvoiceNumber] IN InvoicesForTheseWOs,
        Fact_WorkOrderParts[PartNumber] IN {"ADV", "LEGACY", "*10PROMO"}
    )
```

---

### **MEASURE 4: Labor $ With Inspection (for this Job Code)**

dax

```dax
Labor $ by Job Code = 
VAR CurrentJobCode = SELECTEDVALUE(Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode])
VAR WorkOrdersWithThisJobCode = 
    CALCULATETABLE(
        VALUES(Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber]),
        Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode] = CurrentJobCode,
        Fact_LaborJobSummary[IsInspection] = TRUE
    )
RETURN
    CALCULATE(
        SUM(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoicedLaborAmount]),
        Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber] IN WorkOrdersWithThisJobCode
    )
```

**What this does:**

- Gets work orders with this job code
- Sums ALL labor from those work orders (not just the inspection job code)
- This matches your "Labor With Inspection" logic

---

### **MEASURE 5: Average Parts $ Per Inspection**

dax

```dax
Avg Parts $ by Job Code = 
DIVIDE(
    [Parts $ by Job Code],
    [Inspection Count by Job Code],
    0
)
```

---

### **MEASURE 6: Average Labor $ Per Inspection**

dax

```dax
Avg Labor $ by Job Code = 
DIVIDE(
    [Labor $ by Job Code],
    [Inspection Count by Job Code],
    0
)
```

---

### **MEASURE 7: Total $ Minus Discounts**

dax

```dax
Total $ - Discounts by Job Code = 
[Labor $ by Job Code] + [Parts $ by Job Code] + 
[Labor Discount by Job Code] + [Parts Discount by Job Code]
```

_(You'll need to create Labor Discount by Job Code similar to Parts Discount)_

---

### **MEASURE 8: Average % Discounted**

dax

```dax
Avg % Discounted by Job Code = 
VAR TotalDiscount = ABS([Labor Discount by Job Code] + [Parts Discount by Job Code])
VAR TotalRevenue = [Labor $ by Job Code] + [Parts $ by Job Code]
RETURN
    DIVIDE(TotalDiscount, TotalRevenue, 0)
```

## ⚡ **Performance Issue - Here's Why & Better Solutions:**

### **The Problem:**

Your table is trying to show **EVERY job code** in Fact_LaborJobSummary (thousands of rows including non-inspections), and for each one it's calculating these complex measures. That's why it chokes!

### **✅ SOLUTION 1: Filter in Visual Filters (What you did - works!)**

Adding `IsInspection = TRUE` to the filters pane is perfect! This limits the table to only inspection job codes.

**Keep this!** ✓

---

### **✅ SOLUTION 2: Filter JobCode to Only Inspection Codes (Even Better)**

Instead of showing all job codes and filtering, you can limit the JobCode column itself:

**In the visual Filters pane:**

1. Drag `Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode]` to Filters
2. Switch to "Advanced filtering"
3. Choose "is in"
4. Manually select only your 111 inspection job codes

**OR create a filter measure:**

dax

```dax
Is Inspection Job Code = 
VAR CurrentJobCode = SELECTEDVALUE(Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode])
RETURN
    IF(
        CurrentJobCode IN {
            "IS-CS690 INSPECT",
            "IS-CS770 INSPECT",
            "IS-TRACTOR INSPECT",
            "/INSPECTION",
            "/PLANTER INSPECTION",
            // ... all 111 codes
        },
        1,
        0
    )
```

Then add this to visual filters = 1

### **✅ SOLUTION 3: Use Your JobCodes Table (Best!)**

Since you already have a `JobCodes` table with all 111 inspection codes:

**Create a relationship:**

- From: JobCodes[job_code]
- To: Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode]
- Cardinality: Many-to-One
- Cross-filter: Both (or Single)

**Then in your table visual:**

- Use `JobCodes[job_code]` instead of `Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode]`
- This automatically filters to only inspection codes!
- No need for IsInspection filter!

**This is the cleanest solution!** 🎯

## 🔴 **WHY TOTALS ROW ISN'T SHOWING**

### **The Root Cause:**

Your measures use `SELECTEDVALUE()` at the beginning:

dax

```dax
VAR CurrentJobCode = SELECTEDVALUE(Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode])
```

**Problem:** When Power BI calculates the TOTAL row, there are MULTIPLE job codes selected, so `SELECTEDVALUE()` returns BLANK. This causes all your measures to return BLANK in the totals row, and Power BI hides blank totals rows.

### **The Solution:**

We need to modify your measures to handle the totals row differently. Here's the pattern:

dax

```dax
Inspection Count by Job Code V2 = 
IF(
    HASONEVALUE(Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode]),
    // Single job code selected - use existing logic
    VAR CurrentJobCode = SELECTEDVALUE(Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode])
    VAR WorkOrdersWithThisJobCode = 
        CALCULATETABLE(
            VALUES(Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber]),
            Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode] = CurrentJobCode,
            Fact_LaborJobSummary[IsInspection] = TRUE
        )
    RETURN
        COUNTROWS(WorkOrdersWithThisJobCode),
    // Multiple job codes (totals row) - sum across all
    CALCULATE(
        DISTINCTCOUNT(Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber]),
        Fact_LaborJobSummary[IsInspection] = TRUE
    )
)
```

**BUT** - this would require updating ALL your measures, which is a lot of work.

## 🛠️ **STEP 1: Create Page 2 - Work Order List**

### **The Challenge:**

Your **Fact_LaborJobSummary** has multiple rows per work order:

```
WO 669579 | IS-CS690 INSPECT | $427
WO 669579 | Gen-Electrical   | $385
WO 669579 | DAILY SERVICE    | $290
```

But we need **one row per work order** for the list:

```
WO 669579 | 6/26/2025 | $1,102 labor | $8,530 parts | $9,632 total
```

### **Solution: Create Aggregation Measures**

---

## 📊 **Measures for Work Order List Page:**

### **MEASURE 1: Work Order Labor Total**

dax

```dax
WO Labor Total = 
CALCULATE(
    SUM(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoicedLaborAmount]),
    ALLEXCEPT(Fact_LaborJobSummary, Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber])
)
```

**What this does:** Sums ALL labor for the work order (all job codes)

---

### **MEASURE 2: Work Order Parts Total**

dax

```dax
WO Parts Total = 
VAR CurrentWO = SELECTEDVALUE(Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber])
VAR InvoiceForThisWO = 
    CALCULATE(
        SELECTEDVALUE(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoiceNumber]),
        Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber] = CurrentWO,
        NOT(ISBLANK(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoiceNumber]))
    )
RETURN
    CALCULATE(
        SUM(Fact_WorkOrderParts[SaleValue]),
        Fact_WorkOrderParts[InvoiceNumber] = InvoiceForThisWO,
        Fact_WorkOrderParts[Franchise] <> "ZP",
        NOT(Fact_WorkOrderParts[PartNumber] IN {"ADV", "LEGACY", "4900", "*10PROMO"})
    )
```

**What this does:** Gets parts for this work order's invoice

---

### **MEASURE 3: Work Order Total Revenue**

dax

```dax
WO Total Revenue = 
[WO Labor Total] + [WO Parts Total]
```

---

### **MEASURE 4: Work Order Date** (if you want it as a measure)

dax

```dax
WO Date = 
SELECTEDVALUE(Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderCreationDate])
```

---

## 🎨 **Building Page 2: Work Order List**

### **Step 1: Create a new page**

- Name it: "Work Order List"

### **Step 2: Add a Table visual**

**Columns to show:**

1. **Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber]**
2. **Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderCreationDate]** (or [WO Date] measure)
3. **Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoiceNumber]** (optional but helpful)
4. **[WO Labor Total]** measure
5. **[WO Parts Total]** measure
6. **[WO Total Revenue]** measure

### **Step 3: Remove duplicate work orders**

**The Problem:** You'll see each work order multiple times (once per job code)

**The Solution:** We need to show only ONE row per work order. Power BI doesn't have a built-in "DISTINCT" for table visuals, so we use a workaround:

**Option A: Use a calculated column** (easier) In Fact_LaborJobSummary, create a calculated column:

dax

```dax
IsInspectionJobOnWO = 
VAR CurrentWO = Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber]
VAR CurrentJobCode = Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode]
RETURN
    IF(
        Fact_LaborJobSummary[IsInspection] = TRUE,
        1,
        0
    )
```

Then filter the table visual to only show rows where `IsInspectionJobOnWO = 1`

**Option B: Use a measure to hide duplicates** (more complex) Create a measure:

dax

```dax
Show WO Row = 
VAR CurrentWO = SELECTEDVALUE(Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber])
VAR FirstJobCodeForWO =
```

## 🔍 **The Problem:**

Your count measure isn't respecting the **Branch filter** from the matrix rows!

**Current behavior:**

- Branch 6 row shows: Count = 1
- But there are actually 38 work orders with IS-CS770 INSPECT in Branch 6!

## ✅ **The Fix: Update the Count Measure**

Replace your `Inspection Count by Job Code` measure with this corrected version:

dax

```dax
Inspection Count by Job Code = 
VAR CurrentJobCode = SELECTEDVALUE(Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode])
RETURN
    IF(
        NOT(ISBLANK(CurrentJobCode)),
        CALCULATE(
            DISTINCTCOUNT(Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber]),
            Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode] = CurrentJobCode,
            Fact_LaborJobSummary[IsInspection] = TRUE,
            ALLEXCEPT(
                Fact_LaborJobSummary,
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[BranchCode],
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode]
            )
        ),
        BLANK()
    )
```

**What this does differently:**

- Uses `DISTINCTCOUNT` with `ALLEXCEPT` to properly respect branch context
- Counts unique work orders for the specific Branch + JobCode combination
- Respects all other filters from the matrix visual

This is actually a common issue in data modeling. Let me think about this:

1. **Why it's Many-to-Many:**
    - Fact_LaborJobSummary has multiple rows per invoice (one per job code)

    - Many-to-Many relationships can cause performance issues
    - They can cause unexpected results with CALCULATE and filter context
    - They use a "bridge table" behind the scenes (Power BI creates this automatically)
    - Can lead to inflated numbers if not careful

**GREAT question!** Many-to-Many relationships CAN cause problems - let me explain! 🎯

## 🔴 **Why It's Many-to-Many:**

### **In Fact_LaborJobSummary:**

```
InvoiceNumber | WorkOrderNumber | JobCode
1721413       | 669579          | IS-CS770 INSPECT
1721413       | 669579          | Gen-Electrical
1721413       | 669579          | DAILY SERVICE
```

**InvoiceNumber 1721413 appears 3 times** (one per job code)

### **In Fact_WorkOrderParts:**

```
InvoiceNumber | PartNumber | SaleValue
1721413       | RE535791   | $85
1721413       | AH212366   | $125
1721413       | TY6785     | $200
```

**InvoiceNumber 1721413 appears 3 times** (one per part)

**Result:** Neither side is unique, so it's Many-to-Many

---

## ⚠️ **Potential Problems with Many-to-Many:**

### **Problem 1: Number Inflation**

When you sum across the relationship, numbers can multiply incorrectly:

- 3 job code rows × 3 part rows = 9 combinations
- Could inflate totals by counting things multiple times

### **Problem 2: Performance**

- Power BI creates a hidden "bridge table" behind the scenes
- Slower queries, especially with large datasets
- Can cause report refresh delays

### **Problem 3: Unpredictable Filter Behavior**

- Filters don't always propagate correctly
- Bidirectional filtering required (which you probably set)
- Can cause unexpected results in measures

---

### **Why it's OK here:**

**On Page 3 (Work Order Detail):**

- You're drilling to **ONE work order**
- Which has **ONE invoice**
- So even though the relationship is M:M, you're only ever looking at one invoice at a time
- The multiplication problem doesn't happen

- If yes, the relationship is working correctly!

dax

dax

```dax
            Fact_WorkOrderParts[Franchise] <> "ZP"

    )
```

dax

```dax
    )
```

**AH! That's the issue!** Customer is in the **Parts** table, not the **Labor** table! And it's Many-to-Many because CustomerNumber appears multiple times in Fact_WorkOrderParts (one per part line). 🎯

---

## 🔍 **Why It's Many-to-Many:**

**In Fact_WorkOrderParts:**

```
CustomerNumber | InvoiceNumber | PartNumber | SaleValue
12345          | 1832542       | RE535791   | $85
12345          | 1832542       | AH212366   | $125
12345          | 1832542       | TY6785     | $200
```

**CustomerNumber 12345 appears 3 times** (not unique)

**In dim_CustomerList:**

```
CustomerNumber | PrimaryName
12345          | ZANT, DAVID
```

**IF dim_CustomerList[CustomerNumber] is also not unique** → Many-to-Many

**OR** it could just be that Fact_WorkOrderParts has many rows per customer.

---

## ✅ **SOLUTION: Use a Measure to Look Up Customer**

Since we're on Page 3 and already have the invoice filtered, we can:

1. Get the invoice number from Fact_LaborJobSummary
2. Look up customer number from Fact_WorkOrderParts for that invoice
3. Look up customer name from dim_CustomerList

**Create this measure:**

dax

```dax
Customer Name = 
VAR CurrentInvoice = SELECTEDVALUE(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoiceNumber])
VAR CustomerNum = 
    CALCULATE(
        SELECTEDVALUE(Fact_WorkOrderParts[CustomerNumber]),
        Fact_WorkOrderParts[InvoiceNumber] = CurrentInvoice
    )
RETURN
    IF(
        NOT(ISBLANK(CustomerNum)),
        LOOKUPVALUE(
            dim_CustomerList[PrimaryName],
            dim_CustomerList[CustomerNumber], CustomerNum
        ),
        BLANK()
    )
```

**What this does:**

1. Gets the current invoice (from Page 3 drill-through context)
2. Finds the customer number on that invoice from Fact_WorkOrderParts
3. Looks up the customer name in dim_CustomerList
4. Returns the name

---

**Add a Card visual on Page 3:**

1. Add the `[Customer Name]` measure
2. Drill through from Page 2
3. Should show the customer name!

- If Row Count > Distinct Count → Problem! You have duplicate customers

---

## 🎯 **The Problem:**

**Current rule:**

- > = 0.9 (90%) AND < 1.0 (100%) = Yellow
    
- So 99.6% (0.996) shows yellow even though it's basically at goal

---

## ✅ **SOLUTION OPTIONS:**

### **OPTION 1: Round for Display AND Conditional Formatting (Recommended)**

**Change your % measure to round up at 99.5%+:**

dax

```dax
% to Goal - Inspections = 
VAR ActualPercent = DIVIDE([Total Inspections], [Total Inspection Goal], 0)
RETURN
    IF(ActualPercent >= 0.995, 1, ActualPercent)
```

**What this does:**

- If value is 99.5% or higher → Shows 100%
- If value is less than 99.5% → Shows actual value
- Conditional formatting will now see 100% and make it green!

**Repeat for all 3 % measures:**

- % to Goal - Inspections
- % to Goal - Parts
- % to Goal - Labor With Inspection

---

### **OPTION 2: Adjust Conditional Formatting Threshold**

**Keep your measures as-is, but change the green rule:**

**Current:**

- Green: >= 1.0 (100%)

**Change to:**

- Green: >= 0.99 (99%)

**How to change:**

1. Select matrix
2. Format → Cell elements → Values
3. Find the conditional formatting for background color
4. Edit the **green rule** to be: >= 0.99 instead of >= 1.0

**Result:** 99%+ shows green, under 99% shows yellow/red

---

### **OPTION 3: More Granular Thresholds**

**Create a 4-color scheme:**

- **Dark Green:** >= 1.0 (100%+) → `#10b981`
- **Light Green:** >= 0.99 (99-99.9%) → `#86efac`
- **Yellow:** >= 0.9 (90-98.9%) → `#fbbf24`
- **Red:** < 0.9 (under 90%) → `#ef4444`

**This gives visual distinction between "at goal" and "close to goal"**

---

## 💡 **My Recommendation:**

**Use OPTION 2** - Adjust the green threshold to >= 0.99

**Why:**

- ✅ No need to change measures
- ✅ Quick fix (30 seconds)
- ✅ 99%+ is essentially "at goal"
- ✅ Keeps your actual percentages honest (still displays 99.6%)
- ✅ Makes color coding more forgiving

**If you want to actually DISPLAY 100% instead of 99.6%**, use OPTION 1 (rounds the display)

---

## 🛠️ **Quick Fix (Option 2):**

**For EACH % to Goal column in your matrix:**

1. Select the matrix visual
2. **Format pane** → **Cell elements** → **Values**
3. Find your conditional formatting for **Background color**
4. Click the **green rule**
5. Change from: `value >= 1`
6. To: `value >= 0.99`
7. Click OK

**Repeat for all 3 % columns!**

---

## 🎨 **Optional: Better Rule Structure**

**If you want to use the more nuanced approach:**

**Rule 1 (Dark Green):** value >= 1.0 → `#10b981`  
**Rule 2 (Light Green):** value >= 0.99 → `#86efac`  
**Rule 3 (Yellow):** value >= 0.9 → `#fbbf24`  
**Rule 4 (Red):** value < 0.9 → `#ef4444`

**This gives you:**

- 🟩 100%+ = Dark green (exceeding goal)
- 🟢 99-99.9% = Light green (essentially at goal)
- 🟡 90-98.9% = Yellow (close but not quite)
- 🔴 Under 90% = Red (needs attention)

---

## 📊 **Visual Example:**

- 127% → Green ✓
- 106% → Green ✓
- 100% → Green ✓
- **99.6% → Green ✓** (instead of yellow!)
- 95% → Yellow
- 85% → Red

## 🚀 **Phase 2: Add Estimated Revenue**

This is where it gets exciting! We'll estimate how much revenue these 54 pending inspections will generate when completed.

### **The Logic:**

1. Calculate average revenue per inspection type (from COMPLETED inspections)
2. Multiply by count of PENDING inspections of that type
3. Show estimated revenue

---

## 📊 **STEP 1: Create Average Revenue Measures**

### **Measure 1: Average Inspection Revenue (Completed Only)**

This calculates the average revenue across ALL completed inspections:

dax

```dax
Average Inspection Revenue = 
CALCULATE(
    DIVIDE(
        SUM(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoicedLaborAmount]) + 
        [Parts $ Total],
        DISTINCTCOUNT(Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber])
    ),
    Fact_LaborJobSummary[IsInspection] = TRUE,
    NOT(ISBLANK(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoiceNumber]))
)
```

**What this does:**

- Looks at completed inspections (those with invoice numbers)
- Adds labor + parts revenue
- Divides by count of work orders
- Gives you average revenue per inspection

---

### **Measure 2: Average Revenue by Job Code**

This is more sophisticated - calculates average for EACH inspection type:

dax

```dax
Avg Revenue by Job Code = 
VAR CurrentJobCode = SELECTEDVALUE(Fact_PendingInspections[JobCode])
RETURN
    IF(
        NOT(ISBLANK(CurrentJobCode)),
        CALCULATE(
            DIVIDE(
                SUM(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoicedLaborAmount]) + 
                CALCULATE(
                    [Parts $ Total],
                    Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode] = CurrentJobCode
                ),
                DISTINCTCOUNT(Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber])
            ),
            Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode] = CurrentJobCode,
            Fact_LaborJobSummary[IsInspection] = TRUE,
            NOT(ISBLANK(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoiceNumber]))
        ),
        BLANK()
    )
```

**What this does:**

- For each inspection type (IS-TRACTOR INSPECT, IS-CS690 INSPECT, etc.)
- Calculates average revenue from completed inspections of that type
- Returns the average for that specific job code

---

### **Measure 3: Estimated Revenue for Pending**

This applies the averages to your pending inspections:

dax

```dax
Estimated Revenue - Pending = 
VAR PendingCount = [Total Pending Inspections]
VAR AvgRevenue = [Average Inspection Revenue]
RETURN
    PendingCount * AvgRevenue
```

**What this does:**

- Takes count of pending (54)
- Multiplies by average revenue per inspection
- Gives total estimated revenue

---

### **Measure 4: Estimated Revenue by Job Code (Advanced)**

This is the BEST one - estimates revenue for each pending job code separately:

dax

````dax
Estimated Revenue by Job Code = 
VAR CurrentJobCode = SELECTEDVALUE(Fact_PendingInspections[JobCode])
VAR PendingCountThisCode = 
    CALCULATE(
        COUNTROWS(Fact_PendingInspections),
        Fact_PendingInspections[JobCode] = CurrentJobCode
    )
VAR AvgRevenueThisCode = 
    CALCULATE(
        DIVIDE(
            SUM(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoicedLaborAmount]) + [Parts $ Total],
            DISTINCTCOUNT(Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber])
        ),
        Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode] = CurrentJobCode,
        Fact_LaborJobSummary[IsInspection] = TRUE,
        NOT(ISBLANK(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoiceNumber]))
    )
RETURN
    PendingCountThisCode * AvgRevenueThisCode
```

**What this does:**
- For IS-HARVESTREADY (15 pending):
  - Gets average revenue from completed IS-HARVESTREADY inspections
  - Multiplies 15 × average
  - Shows estimated revenue for those 15
- Does this for each job code!
````

## 🔍 **What's Going Wrong:**

The `[Avg Revenue by Job Code]` measure is calculating **TOTAL revenue** instead of **AVERAGE revenue per work order**.

**The issue is likely:**

1. **Parts filtering isn't working correctly** - it's summing ALL parts instead of just parts for that job code

## ✅ **THE FIX: Revised Measure**

Let me give you a **better approach** that properly connects labor + parts by work order:

dax

```dax
Avg Revenue by Job Code = 
VAR CurrentJobCode = SELECTEDVALUE(Fact_PendingInspections[JobCode])
RETURN
    IF(
        NOT(ISBLANK(CurrentJobCode)),
        // Get all completed work orders with this job code
        VAR CompletedWOs = 
            CALCULATETABLE(
                VALUES(Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber]),
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode] = CurrentJobCode,
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[IsInspection] = TRUE,
                NOT(ISBLANK(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoiceNumber]))
            )
        
        // Get invoices for those work orders
        VAR InvoicesForWOs = 
            CALCULATETABLE(
                VALUES(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoiceNumber]),
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber] IN CompletedWOs,
                NOT(ISBLANK(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoiceNumber]))
            )
        
        // Calculate total labor for these work orders
        VAR TotalLabor = 
            CALCULATE(
                SUM(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoicedLaborAmount]),
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber] IN CompletedWOs
            )
        
        // Calculate total parts for these invoices
        VAR TotalParts = 
            CALCULATE(
                SUM(Fact_WorkOrderParts[SaleValue]),
                Fact_WorkOrderParts[InvoiceNumber] IN InvoicesForWOs,
                Fact_WorkOrderParts[Franchise] <> "ZP",
                NOT(Fact_WorkOrderParts[PartNumber] IN {"ADV", "LEGACY", "4900", "*10PROMO"})
            )
        
        // Count of work orders
        VAR WOCount = COUNTROWS(CompletedWOs)
        
        RETURN
            DIVIDE(TotalLabor + TotalParts, WOCount, 0)
        ,
        BLANK()
    )
```

**What this does differently:**

1. ✅ Finds all completed work orders with this job code
2. ✅ Gets their invoice numbers
3. ✅ Sums labor from those work orders
4. ✅ Sums parts from those invoices (using the same filter logic as your other measures)
5. ✅ Divides by work order count for true average

## 🛠️ **STEP 1: Create the Base Measures**

### **Measure 1: Count of Completed Inspections (for selected JobCode)**

dax

```dax
Completed Inspections - Selected JobCode = 
VAR SelectedJobCode = SELECTEDVALUE(Fact_PendingInspections[JobCode])
RETURN
    IF(
        NOT(ISBLANK(SelectedJobCode)),
        CALCULATE(
            DISTINCTCOUNT(Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber]),
            Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode] = SelectedJobCode,
            Fact_LaborJobSummary[IsInspection] = TRUE,
            NOT(ISBLANK(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoiceNumber]))
        ),
        BLANK()
    )
```

**What this does:** Counts how many completed inspections of this type we have historically

---

### **Measure 2: Times This Part Was Sold on This Inspection Type**

dax

```dax
Part Sold Count - For JobCode = 
VAR SelectedJobCode = SELECTEDVALUE(Fact_PendingInspections[JobCode])
VAR CurrentPart = SELECTEDVALUE(Fact_WorkOrderParts[PartNumber])
RETURN
    IF(
        NOT(ISBLANK(SelectedJobCode)) && NOT(ISBLANK(CurrentPart)),
        // Get completed work orders with this job code
        VAR CompletedWOs = 
            CALCULATETABLE(
                VALUES(Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber]),
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode] = SelectedJobCode,
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[IsInspection] = TRUE,
                NOT(ISBLANK(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoiceNumber]))
            )
        
        // Get invoices for those work orders
        VAR InvoicesForWOs = 
            CALCULATETABLE(
                VALUES(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoiceNumber]),
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber] IN CompletedWOs,
                NOT(ISBLANK(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoiceNumber]))
            )
        
        // Count distinct invoices where this part was sold
        VAR PartSoldCount = 
            CALCULATE(
                DISTINCTCOUNT(Fact_WorkOrderParts[InvoiceNumber]),
                Fact_WorkOrderParts[InvoiceNumber] IN InvoicesForWOs,
                Fact_WorkOrderParts[PartNumber] = CurrentPart,
                Fact_WorkOrderParts[Franchise] <> "ZP"
            )
        
        RETURN PartSoldCount
        ,
        BLANK()
    )
```

**What this does:** Counts how many times this specific part was sold on completed inspections of this type

---

### **Measure 3: Frequency Percentage**

dax

```dax
Part Frequency % - For JobCode = 
DIVIDE(
    [Part Sold Count - For JobCode],
    [Completed Inspections - Selected JobCode],
    0
)
```

**What this does:** Calculates: "Air filter sold on 85% of IS-TRACTOR INSPECT jobs"

---

### **Measure 4: Average Quantity Per Occurrence**

dax

```dax
Avg Part Quantity - For JobCode = 
VAR SelectedJobCode = SELECTEDVALUE(Fact_PendingInspections[JobCode])
VAR CurrentPart = SELECTEDVALUE(Fact_WorkOrderParts[PartNumber])
RETURN
    IF(
        NOT(ISBLANK(SelectedJobCode)) && NOT(ISBLANK(CurrentPart)),
        VAR CompletedWOs = 
            CALCULATETABLE(
                VALUES(Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber]),
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode] = SelectedJobCode,
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[IsInspection] = TRUE,
                NOT(ISBLANK(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoiceNumber]))
            )
        
        VAR InvoicesForWOs = 
            CALCULATETABLE(
                VALUES(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoiceNumber]),
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber] IN CompletedWOs,
                NOT(ISBLANK(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoiceNumber]))
            )
        
        VAR TotalQty = 
            CALCULATE(
                SUM(Fact_WorkOrderParts[Quantity]),
                Fact_WorkOrderParts[InvoiceNumber] IN InvoicesForWOs,
                Fact_WorkOrderParts[PartNumber] = CurrentPart,
                Fact_WorkOrderParts[Franchise] <> "ZP"
            )
        
        VAR TimesUsed = [Part Sold Count - For JobCode]
        
        RETURN DIVIDE(TotalQty, TimesUsed, 0)
        ,
        BLANK()
    )
```

**What this does:** When we sell this part, how many do we sell on average? (2.1 filters per inspection)

---

### **Measure 5: Estimated Quantity Needed for Pending**

dax

````dax
Est Quantity Needed - For Pending = 
VAR PendingCount = 
    CALCULATE(
        COUNTROWS(Fact_PendingInspections),
        ALLEXCEPT(Fact_PendingInspections, Fact_PendingInspections[JobCode])
    )
VAR Frequency = [Part Frequency % - For JobCode]
VAR AvgQty = [Avg Part Quantity - For JobCode]
RETURN
    PendingCount * Frequency * AvgQty
```

**What this does:** "14 pending × 85% frequency × 2.1 avg qty = 25 filters needed"
````

## 🔍 **The Problem:**

The table needs to know **WHICH parts to show**. Right now it has:

- ❌ No base columns from Fact_WorkOrderParts (no PartNumber rows to iterate)
- ❌ Just measures (but measures need rows to calculate against)

## ✅ **THE FIX: Add Base Columns + Filter Measure**

### **STEP 1: Create a Filter Measure**

This determines if a part should be shown for the selected inspection type:

dax

````dax
Show Part for JobCode = 
VAR SelectedJobCode = SELECTEDVALUE(Fact_PendingInspections[JobCode])
VAR CurrentPart = SELECTEDVALUE(Fact_WorkOrderParts[PartNumber])
RETURN
    IF(
        NOT(ISBLANK(SelectedJobCode)) && NOT(ISBLANK(CurrentPart)),
        IF([Part Sold Count - For JobCode] > 0, 1, 0),
        0
    )
```

**What this does:** Returns 1 if this part was ever sold on the selected inspection type, 0 if not

---

### **STEP 2: Rebuild Your Parts Table**

**In your parts table visual:**

1. **FIRST, add these base columns** (this creates rows to iterate):
   - Fact_WorkOrderParts[PartNumber]
   - Fact_WorkOrderParts[PartDescription]

2. **THEN add your measures:**
   - [Part Sold Count - For JobCode]
   - [Part Frequency % - For JobCode]
   - [Avg Part Quantity - For JobCode]
   - [Est Quantity Needed - For Pending]

3. **NOW add the filter** (this hides irrelevant parts):
   - Go to **Filters pane**
   - Drag **[Show Part for JobCode]** to "Filters on this visual"
   - Set to: **= 1**

---

## 🧪 **Why This Works:**

**Without base columns:**
```
Table: (empty)
└─ Measures try to calculate but have no rows
└─ Result: Blank table
```

**With base columns + filter:**
```
Table: All parts from Fact_WorkOrderParts
├─ PartNumber: RE535791
│  └─ Measures calculate for RE535791 on selected job code
│  └─ Filter measure: Was this part sold? Yes = 1, show it
├─ PartNumber: AH212366
│  └─ Measures calculate for AH212366 on selected job code
│  └─ Filter measure: Was this part sold? Yes = 1, show it
├─ PartNumber: XYZ999
│  └─ Measures calculate for XYZ999 on selected job code
│  └─ Filter measure: Was this part sold? No = 0, hide it
````

dax

````dax
        IF([Part Sold Count - For JobCode] > 0, 1, 0),
````

```
Part AHC21430 (aggregated across all invoices)
```

```dax
)
```

2. **Update the measures to use ALLEXCEPT:**

The issue is that measures are calculating per row (part+invoice) instead of per part. We need to force aggregation at part level.

**Updated Part Sold Count measure:**

dax

````dax
Part Sold Count - For JobCode = 
VAR SelectedJobCode = SELECTEDVALUE(Fact_PendingInspections[JobCode])
VAR CurrentPart = SELECTEDVALUE(Fact_WorkOrderParts[PartNumber])
RETURN
    IF(
        NOT(ISBLANK(SelectedJobCode)) && NOT(ISBLANK(CurrentPart)),
        CALCULATE(
            // Get completed work orders with this job code
            VAR CompletedWOs = 
                CALCULATETABLE(
                    VALUES(Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber]),
                    Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode] = SelectedJobCode,
                    Fact_LaborJobSummary[IsInspection] = TRUE,
                    NOT(ISBLANK(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoiceNumber]))
                )
            
            // Get invoices for those work orders
            VAR InvoicesForWOs = 
                CALCULATETABLE(
                    VALUES(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoiceNumber]),
                    Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber] IN CompletedWOs,
                    NOT(ISBLANK(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoiceNumber]))
                )
            
            // Count distinct invoices where THIS SPECIFIC PART was sold
            VAR PartSoldCount = 
                CALCULATE(
                    DISTINCTCOUNT(Fact_WorkOrderParts[InvoiceNumber]),
                    Fact_WorkOrderParts[InvoiceNumber] IN InvoicesForWOs,
                    Fact_WorkOrderParts[PartNumber] = CurrentPart,
                    Fact_WorkOrderParts[Franchise] <> "ZP",
                    ALLEXCEPT(Fact_WorkOrderParts, Fact_WorkOrderParts[PartNumber])
                )
            
            RETURN PartSoldCount,
            
            BLANK()
        ),
        BLANK()
    )
```
````

## 🛠️ **STEP 1: Create Service Recommendation Measures**

### **Measure 1: Count of Work Orders with Other Services**

dax

```dax
Service Count - For JobCode = 
VAR SelectedInspectionCode = SELECTEDVALUE(Fact_PendingInspections[JobCode])
VAR CurrentServiceCode = SELECTEDVALUE(Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode])
RETURN
    IF(
        NOT(ISBLANK(SelectedInspectionCode)) && NOT(ISBLANK(CurrentServiceCode)),
        // Get work orders that have the selected inspection
        VAR WorkOrdersWithInspection = 
            CALCULATETABLE(
                VALUES(Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber]),
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode] = SelectedInspectionCode,
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[IsInspection] = TRUE,
                NOT(ISBLANK(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoiceNumber]))
            )
        
        // Count how many of those work orders ALSO have the current service
        VAR ServiceCount = 
            CALCULATE(
                DISTINCTCOUNT(Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber]),
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber] IN WorkOrdersWithInspection,
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode] = CurrentServiceCode,
                // Exclude the inspection itself from the count
                CurrentServiceCode <> SelectedInspectionCode
            )
        
        RETURN ServiceCount
        ,
        BLANK()
    )
```

**What this does:** Counts how many work orders had both the inspection AND this other service

---

### **Measure 2: Service Frequency Percentage**

dax

```dax
Service Frequency % - For JobCode = 
DIVIDE(
    [Service Count - For JobCode],
    [Completed Inspections - Selected JobCode],
    0
)
```

**What this does:** "Gen-Electrical appears on 42% of tractor inspection work orders"

---

### **Measure 3: Average Labor $ for This Service**

dax

```dax
Avg Labor $ - For Service = 
VAR SelectedInspectionCode = SELECTEDVALUE(Fact_PendingInspections[JobCode])
VAR CurrentServiceCode = SELECTEDVALUE(Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode])
RETURN
    IF(
        NOT(ISBLANK(SelectedInspectionCode)) && NOT(ISBLANK(CurrentServiceCode)),
        VAR WorkOrdersWithInspection = 
            CALCULATETABLE(
                VALUES(Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber]),
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode] = SelectedInspectionCode,
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[IsInspection] = TRUE,
                NOT(ISBLANK(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoiceNumber]))
            )
        
        // Calculate average labor for this service on those work orders
        VAR TotalLabor = 
            CALCULATE(
                SUM(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoicedLaborAmount]),
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber] IN WorkOrdersWithInspection,
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode] = CurrentServiceCode
            )
        
        VAR ServiceCount = [Service Count - For JobCode]
        
        RETURN DIVIDE(TotalLabor, ServiceCount, 0)
        ,
        BLANK()
    )
```

**What this does:** "When Gen-Electrical is added to a tractor inspection, it averages $385 in labor"

---

### **Measure 4: Estimated Service Opportunities for Pending**

dax

```dax
Est Service Opportunities = 
VAR PendingCount = 
    CALCULATE(
        COUNTROWS(Fact_PendingInspections),
        ALLEXCEPT(Fact_PendingInspections, Fact_PendingInspections[JobCode])
    )
VAR Frequency = [Service Frequency % - For JobCode]
RETURN
    PendingCount * Frequency
```

**What this does:** "14 pending tractors × 42% frequency = 6 will likely need Gen-Electrical too"

---

### **Measure 5: Estimated Additional Revenue from Services**

dax

```dax
Est Service Revenue = 
[Est Service Opportunities] * [Avg Labor $ - For Service]
```

**What this does:** "6 electrical services × $385 = $2,310 additional revenue opportunity"

---

### **Measure 6: Filter Measure for Services**

dax

````dax
Show Service for JobCode = 
VAR SelectedInspectionCode = SELECTEDVALUE(Fact_PendingInspections[JobCode])
VAR CurrentServiceCode = SELECTEDVALUE(Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode])
RETURN
    IF(
        NOT(ISBLANK(SelectedInspectionCode)) && NOT(ISBLANK(CurrentServiceCode)),
        // Don't show the inspection itself
        IF(
            CurrentServiceCode <> SelectedInspectionCode && 
            [Service Count - For JobCode] > 0,
            1,
            0
        ),
        0
    )
```

**What this does:** Filters table to only show services that were actually added (not the inspection itself)
````

## ✅ **THE FIX: Corrected Measure**

Replace your **Service Count - For JobCode** measure with this corrected version:

dax

```dax
Service Count - For JobCode = 
VAR SelectedInspectionCode = SELECTEDVALUE(Fact_PendingInspections[JobCode])
VAR CurrentServiceCode = SELECTEDVALUE(Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode])
RETURN
    IF(
        NOT(ISBLANK(SelectedInspectionCode)) && 
        NOT(ISBLANK(CurrentServiceCode)) &&
        CurrentServiceCode <> SelectedInspectionCode,  // Check this OUTSIDE the CALCULATE
        
        // Get work orders that have the selected inspection
        VAR WorkOrdersWithInspection = 
            CALCULATETABLE(
                VALUES(Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber]),
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode] = SelectedInspectionCode,
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[IsInspection] = TRUE,
                NOT(ISBLANK(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoiceNumber]))
            )
        
        // Count how many of those work orders ALSO have the current service
        VAR ServiceCount = 
            CALCULATE(
                DISTINCTCOUNT(Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber]),
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber] IN WorkOrdersWithInspection,
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode] = CurrentServiceCode
            )
        
        RETURN ServiceCount
        ,
        BLANK()
    )
```

**What I changed:**

- ❌ Removed the problematic filter inside CALCULATE
- ✅ Moved the comparison to the IF statement at the top
- ✅ Now it checks if CurrentServiceCode ≠ SelectedInspectionCode BEFORE doing any calculations

## 🎯 **Why This Error Happened:**

**Original problematic line:**

dax

```dax
CALCULATE(
    ...,
    CurrentServiceCode <> SelectedInspectionCode  // ❌ Error!
)
```

**Problem:**

- DAX filter expressions in CALCULATE must reference a column
- `CurrentServiceCode <> SelectedInspectionCode` compares two scalar values
- No column reference = error!

**Solution:**

dax

```dax
IF(
    CurrentServiceCode <> SelectedInspectionCode,  // ✅ Outside CALCULATE
    CALCULATE(...)
)
```

**Now:** The comparison happens before filtering, not as a filter expression

## ✅ **SOLUTION: Pre-Calculated Table Approach**

Instead of calculating in real-time (slow), let's **pre-calculate** the service recommendations once and use that table (fast)!

### **Create a Calculated Table:**

**Go to Modeling → New Table**

dax

```dax
ServiceRecommendations = 
VAR InspectionCodes = VALUES(Fact_PendingInspections[JobCode])

RETURN
GENERATE(
    InspectionCodes,
    VAR CurrentInspection = Fact_PendingInspections[JobCode]
    
    // Get all work orders with this inspection
    VAR WorkOrdersWithInspection = 
        CALCULATETABLE(
            VALUES(Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber]),
            Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode] = CurrentInspection,
            Fact_LaborJobSummary[IsInspection] = TRUE,
            NOT(ISBLANK(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoiceNumber]))
        )
    
    // Count completed inspections
    VAR CompletedCount = COUNTROWS(WorkOrdersWithInspection)
    
    RETURN
    ADDCOLUMNS(
        // Get all OTHER services on those work orders
        CALCULATETABLE(
            SUMMARIZE(
                Fact_LaborJobSummary,
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode],
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobType]
            ),
            Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber] IN WorkOrdersWithInspection,
            Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode] <> CurrentInspection,
            Fact_LaborJobSummary[IsInspection] = FALSE
        ),
        
        "InspectionJobCode", CurrentInspection,
        "CompletedInspections", CompletedCount,
        "TimesServiceAdded", 
            CALCULATE(
                DISTINCTCOUNT(Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber]),
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber] IN WorkOrdersWithInspection,
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode] = EARLIER(Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode])
            ),
        "TotalServiceLabor",
            CALCULATE(
                SUM(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoicedLaborAmount]),
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber] IN WorkOrdersWithInspection,
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode] = EARLIER(Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode])
            )
    )
)
```

```dax
        // Count WOs that also have the service
        RETURN
        CALCULATE(
            DISTINCTCOUNT(Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber]),
            Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber] IN WOs,
            Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode] = ServiceCode
```

## 🛠️ **STEP-BY-STEP: Create the Pre-Calculated Table**

### **STEP 1: Create the Calculated Table**

**Go to: Modeling → New Table**

**Paste this code:**

dax

````dax
ServiceRecommendations = 
// Get list of all inspection job codes
VAR InspectionCodes = 
    DISTINCT(Fact_PendingInspections[JobCode])

RETURN
// For each inspection code, find associated services
GENERATE(
    InspectionCodes,
    
    VAR CurrentInspection = [JobCode]
    
    // Get work orders with this inspection
    VAR InspectionWorkOrders = 
        CALCULATETABLE(
            VALUES(Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber]),
            Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode] = CurrentInspection,
            Fact_LaborJobSummary[IsInspection] = TRUE,
            NOT(ISBLANK(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoiceNumber]))
        )
    
    // Count of completed inspections
    VAR CompletedCount = COUNTROWS(InspectionWorkOrders)
    
    // Get all services (non-inspections) on those work orders
    VAR ServicesOnTheseWOs = 
        CALCULATETABLE(
            SUMMARIZE(
                Fact_LaborJobSummary,
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode],
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobType]
            ),
            Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber] IN InspectionWorkOrders,
            Fact_LaborJobSummary[IsInspection] = FALSE
        )
    
    RETURN
    ADDCOLUMNS(
        ServicesOnTheseWOs,
        
        "InspectionJobCode", CurrentInspection,
        "CompletedInspections", CompletedCount,
        
        // Count how many WOs had this service
        "TimesAdded", 
            CALCULATE(
                DISTINCTCOUNT(Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber]),
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber] IN InspectionWorkOrders
            ),
        
        // Total labor for this service on those WOs
        "TotalLabor",
            CALCULATE(
                SUM(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoicedLaborAmount]),
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber] IN InspectionWorkOrders
            )
    )
)
```
````

```dax
)
```

**This means:** Instead of showing "236 out of 561 = 42%", it's showing something like "26,569 / 561 = 2660%"

### **Problem 2: Times Added Is Too High**

- **GEN REPAIR 1:** 26,569 times (but only 561 completed tractors?!)
- **Should be:** Maybe 200-300 times (if it appears on 40% of inspections)

### **Problem 3: Revenue Estimates Are Astronomical**

- **Est Service Revenue card:** $870,902.04 for 14 pending inspections
- **That's:** $62,207 per inspection in additional services!
- **Should be:** Maybe $15,000-$25,000 total for 14 inspections

---

## 🔍 **ROOT CAUSE:**

The `ServiceRecommendations` calculated table is counting **labor ROWS** instead of distinct **work orders**.

**What's happening:**

- If GEN REPAIR 1 has 10 labor rows per work order (multiple techs, multiple days)
- And it appears on 200 work orders
- It's counting: 200 × 10 = 2,000 labor rows ❌
- Should count: 200 work orders ✓

---

## ✅ **THE FIX: Correct the ServiceRecommendations Table**

**Delete the ServiceRecommendations table and recreate with this fix:**

dax

````dax
ServiceRecommendations = 
VAR InspectionCodes = 
    SELECTCOLUMNS(
        DISTINCT(Fact_PendingInspections[JobCode]),
        "InspectionJobCode", Fact_PendingInspections[JobCode]
    )

RETURN
GENERATE(
    InspectionCodes,
    
    VAR CurrentInspection = [InspectionJobCode]
    
    // Get work orders with this inspection
    VAR InspectionWorkOrders = 
        CALCULATETABLE(
            VALUES(Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber]),
            Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode] = CurrentInspection,
            Fact_LaborJobSummary[IsInspection] = TRUE,
            NOT(ISBLANK(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoiceNumber]))
        )
    
    VAR CompletedCount = COUNTROWS(InspectionWorkOrders)
    
    // Get unique services (one row per service)
    VAR UniqueServices = 
        CALCULATETABLE(
            SUMMARIZE(
                Fact_LaborJobSummary,
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode],
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobType]
            ),
            Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber] IN InspectionWorkOrders,
            Fact_LaborJobSummary[IsInspection] = FALSE
        )
    
    RETURN
    ADDCOLUMNS(
        UniqueServices,
        
        "CompletedInspections", CompletedCount,
        
        // FIXED: Count distinct work orders with this service
        "TimesAdded", 
            VAR ServiceCode = Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode]
            VAR WorkOrdersWithService = 
                CALCULATETABLE(
                    VALUES(Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber]),
                    Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber] IN InspectionWorkOrders,
                    Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode] = ServiceCode
                )
            RETURN
                COUNTROWS(WorkOrdersWithService),
        
        // FIXED: Total labor for this service (all rows combined)
        "TotalLabor",
            VAR ServiceCode = Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode]
            RETURN
            CALCULATE(
                SUM(Fact_LaborJobSummary[InvoicedLaborAmount]),
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[WorkOrderNumber] IN InspectionWorkOrders,
                Fact_LaborJobSummary[JobCode] = ServiceCode
            )
    )
)
```

**Key changes:**
- ✅ Used `CALCULATETABLE(VALUES(...))` to get distinct work orders first
- ✅ Then `COUNTROWS()` to count them
- ✅ This ensures we count work orders, not labor lines
````

## ✅ **SOLUTION 1: Fix the Source Table (BEST)**

**Update your Fact_PendingInspections table to replace NULL with 0:**

**Go to: Home → Transform Data → Find Fact_PendingInspections query**

**Find this section in your query** (near the end where you expand hours):

m

```m
ExpandHours = Table.ExpandTableColumn(
    JoinHours,
    "Hours",
    {"HoursWorked"},
    {"HoursWorked"}
),
```

**Add this step right after it:**

m

```m
// Replace NULL hours with 0
ReplaceNullHours = Table.ReplaceValue(
    ExpandHours,
    null,
    0,
    Replacer.ReplaceValue,
    {"HoursWorked"}
),
```

**Then update the final step to reference ReplaceNullHours instead of ExpandHours.**

**Original final step:**

m

```m
SetDataTypes = Table.TransformColumnTypes(
    AddIsInspection,  // or whatever the previous step was
    ...
)
```

**Make sure it flows through the new step:**

m

```m
AddIsInspection = Table.AddColumn(
    ReplaceNullHours,  // ← Changed to use the step with replaced nulls
    "IsInspection",
    each true,
    type logical
),
```

## 🎨 **HTML CARD 2: Pending Inspection Types Summary**

**Create this measure:**

dax

````dax
Pending Inspection Types HTML = 
// Get top 5 pending inspection types
VAR TopInspections = 
    TOPN(
        5,
        ADDCOLUMNS(
            SUMMARIZE(
                Fact_PendingInspections,
                Fact_PendingInspections[JobCode]
            ),
            "@Count", CALCULATE(COUNTROWS(Fact_PendingInspections)),
            "@EstRev", [Avg Revenue by Job Code] * CALCULATE(COUNTROWS(Fact_PendingInspections))
        ),
        [@Count],
        DESC
    )

// Build HTML for each inspection type
VAR InspectionCards = 
    CONCATENATEX(
        TopInspections,
        VAR JobCode = Fact_PendingInspections[JobCode]
        VAR Count = [@Count]
        VAR EstRev = [@EstRev]
        VAR EstRevText = FORMAT(EstRev / 1000, "$#,##0.0") & "K"
        VAR JobCodeShort = 
            SWITCH(
                TRUE(),
                CONTAINSSTRING(JobCode, "TRACTOR"), "🚜 Tractor",
                CONTAINSSTRING(JobCode, "HARVESTREADY"), "🌾 Harvest Ready",
                CONTAINSSTRING(JobCode, "CS690"), "🌽 CS690 Combine",
                CONTAINSSTRING(JobCode, "CS770"), "🌽 CS770 Combine",
                CONTAINSSTRING(JobCode, "STRIPPER"), "🧹 Stripper",
                CONTAINSSTRING(JobCode, "COMPACT"), "🏗️ Compact",
                CONTAINSSTRING(JobCode, "SPRAYER"), "💧 Sprayer",
                "📋 " & JobCode
            )
        RETURN
        "
        <div style='
            background: white;
            padding: 20px;
            border-radius: 8px;
            margin-bottom: 15px;
            box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.1);
            display: flex;
            justify-content: space-between;
            align-items: center;
            border-left: 5px solid #3A7CA5;
        '>
            <div style='flex: 2;'>
                <div style='font-size: 18px; font-weight: 600; color: #1D3C4E; margin-bottom: 5px;'>
````

### **Measure 2: Branch Performance Cards**

dax

```dax
Branch Performance Cards HTML = 
// Get all branches with their performance
VAR BranchData = 
    ADDCOLUMNS(
        SUMMARIZE(
            ALLSELECTED(Fact_LaborJobSummary),
            Fact_LaborJobSummary[BranchCode],
            Fact_LaborJobSummary[Branch]
        ),
        "@Inspections", [Total Inspections],
        "@InspGoal", [Total Inspection Goal],
        "@InspPct", [% to Goal - Inspections],
        "@PartsTotal", [Parts $ Total],
        "@PartsGoal", [Parts $ Goal],
        "@PartsPct", [% to Goal - Parts],
        "@LaborTotal", [Labor With Inspection],
        "@LaborGoal", [Total Labor Goal With Inspection],
        "@LaborPct", [% to Goal - Labor With Inspection]
    )

// Separate into performance tiers
VAR TopPerformers = FILTER(BranchData, [@InspPct] >= 1.2)
VAR OnTrack = FILTER(BranchData, [@InspPct] >= 1.0 && [@InspPct] < 1.2)
VAR NeedsAttention = FILTER(BranchData, [@InspPct] < 1.0)

// Build cards for top performers
VAR TopCards = 
    CONCATENATEX(
        TopPerformers,
        VAR BranchName = Fact_LaborJobSummary[Branch]
        VAR InspPct = [@InspPct]
        VAR PartsPct = [@PartsPct]
        VAR LaborPct = [@LaborPct]
        VAR Inspections = [@Inspections]
        VAR InspGoal = [@InspGoal]
        VAR PartsTotal = [@PartsTotal]
        VAR LaborTotal = [@LaborTotal]
        
        RETURN
        "
        <div style='
            background: white;
            padding: 20px;
            border-radius: 8px;
            margin-bottom: 15px;
            box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.1);
            border-left: 5px solid #4ade80;
        '>
            <div style='display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 15px;'>
                <div>
                    <div style='font-size: 20px; font-weight: 700; color: #1D3C4E;'>
                        " & BranchName & "
                    </div>
                    <div style='font-size: 14px; color: #6B7280;'>
                        " & FORMAT(Inspections, "#,##0") & " inspections (Goal: " & FORMAT(InspGoal, "#,##0") & ")
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div style='text-align: right;'>
                    <div style='font-size: 36px; font-weight: 700; color: #4ade80;'>
                        " & FORMAT(InspPct, "0%") & "
                    </div>
                    <div style='font-size: 12px; color: #6B7280;'>
                        Overall Performance
                    </div>
                </div>
            </div>
            
            <div style='display: flex; gap: 20px; padding-top: 15px; border-top: 1px solid #e5e7eb;'>
                <div style='flex: 1; text-align: center;'>
                    <div style='font-size: 11px; color: #6B7280; text-transform: uppercase; margin-bottom: 5px;'>Parts</div>
                    <div style='font-size: 18px; font-weight: 700; color: #3A7CA5;'>
                        " & FORMAT(PartsTotal/1000, "$#,##0") & "K
                    </div>
                    <div style='font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; color: " & IF(PartsPct >= 1, "#4ade80", "#ef4444") & ";'>
                        " & FORMAT(PartsPct, "0%") & "
                    </div>
                </div>
                
                <div style='flex: 1; text-align: center;'>
                    <div style='font-size: 11px; color: #6B7280; text-transform: uppercase; margin-bottom: 5px;'>Labor</div>
                    <div style='font-size: 18px; font-weight: 700; color: #3A7CA5;'>
                        " & FORMAT(LaborTotal/1000, "$#,##0") & "K
                    </div>
                    <div style='font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; color: " & IF(LaborPct >= 1, "#4ade80", "#ef4444") & ";'>
                        " & FORMAT(LaborPct, "0%") & "
                    </div>
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>
        ",
        "",
        [@InspPct],
        DESC
    )

RETURN
"
<div style='font-family: Segoe UI, Arial, sans-serif;'>
    <div style='
        font-size: 22px; 
        font-weight: 700; 
        color: #1D3C4E; 
        margin-bottom: 20px;
        padding: 15px 20px;
        background: linear-gradient(to right, #4ade80, #22c55e);
        color: white;
        border-radius: 8px;
        box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.1);
    '>
        🏆 TOP PERFORMERS (120%+ to Goal)
    </div>
    
    " & TopCards & "
</div>
"
```
